confound_and_correction.what_happened: First Ollama run (no extra_body, matching the llama-server run 1:1) FAILED property (a): tool_calls empty, finish_reason=length. Reading the verbatim response showed the model was still mid chain-of-thought (message.reasoning, ~500+ words) when max_tokens=512 was hit — Qwen3 thinking defaults to ON via Ollama and the reasoning trace alone can exceed the budget before any tool_call is emitted.
confound_and_correction.why_it_is_not_a_roundtrip_defect: This is a token-budget/thinking-mode confound, not a wire-format flattening defect — content was empty (not a flattened tool-call blob) and finish_reason=length, not stop/tool_calls. Research-capture requirement 9 explicitly calls for non-thinking mode on the tool lane for exactly this reason.
confound_and_correction.correction_applied: Re-ran with --extra-body {"think": false} (Ollama native OpenAI-compat field) and max_tokens raised 512->1024 for probe (a). Result: PASS, tool_calls returned in 134 completion tokens. This corrected run is the one recorded in stacks[].result above; the raw confounded run is preserved for audit at evidence/b4a-serving-roundtrip-ollama-v1-thinking-confound.json.
confound_and_correction.lesson_for_the_gate_itself: A fair stack comparison must control for each stack own thinking-disable mechanism (llama.cpp: --reasoning off at server launch; Ollama: think:false per-request) — testing one with thinking off and the other with thinking on would have produced a false asymmetric verdict.

cross_stack_finding.summary: Both stacks PASS (a) native structured tool_calls, (b) history round-trip with assistant.tool_calls preserved, (c) role:tool acceptance. Both stacks FAIL (d): parallel_tool_calls=false is accepted in the request body without a validation error but is NOT enforced by either server — both returned 2 tool_calls in a single turn on a prompt designed to invite two.
cross_stack_finding.implication_for_F4_team_bot: Neither serving layer can be trusted to cap tool calls per turn on its own. The MANDATE F4 requirement (single tool per turn, parallel_tool_calls=false) MUST be enforced at the application layer regardless of stack choice: execute only tool_calls[0] from any response and explicitly ignore/reject the rest — never assume the server already limited it. This is a build requirement for apps/team-bot/, not a stack selection criterion (it does not favor llama.cpp over Ollama since both fail it identically).
cross_stack_finding.reproducibility: llama.cpp re-run on a freshly restarted, independent server process/model-load — identical outcome both times (a/b/c PASS, d FAIL, same 2-tool response shape). Not a one-off fluke.

gate_verdict.note: F8 binding gate text is: server MUST round-trip native tools/tool_calls/role:tool WITHOUT flattening to text — that is properties a/b/c, and BOTH stacks pass all three empirically. Property (d) (parallel_tool_calls honored) is a distinct requirement from research-capture item 5, and its failure on both stacks is a finding for the application layer (F4), not a disqualifier between llama.cpp and Ollama.
